interface.name: deck_widget_manager_v1
interface.description: Global interface for Deck widget management. Widgets bind to this interface to obtain a deck_widget_surface_v1 for their wl_surface. The compositor identifies the connecting widget via SO_PEERCRED on the Wayland socket — there is no out-of-band identity handshake.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the widget manager. Does not affect existing widget surfaces.

request.name: get_widget_surface
request.description: Create a deck_widget_surface_v1 for the given wl_surface. The compositor identifies the widget from the peer credentials of the Wayland connection and emits initial configuration (configure, params, setting events, configure_done) against the new surface. The wl_surface must not already have a role.

entry.name: unknown_client
entry.summary: compositor has no initial config for this client

interface.name: deck_widget_surface_v1
interface.description:
Interface for a widget surface. On surface creation, the compositor emits initial configuration as a sequence of events, terminated by configure_done:
configure(size_type, width, height) display_info(display_width, display_height, display_shape, dpi) params(json) timezone / night_mode / date_format / ... (setting events) configure_done
The widget must wait for configure_done before starting to render. After configure_done, the same setting events continue to flow whenever system settings change. Widget readiness is detected when the first buffer is committed.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the widget surface role. The wl_surface remains valid.

request.name: play_sound
request.description: Ask the compositor to play a system sound. The sound must be one of the names registered with the compositor's sound manager.

request.name: led_temporary

description.summary: run an LED effect for a finite duration

request.description: The compositor will run the given effect for `duration_ms` milliseconds, then return to whatever LED state was active before the request.

request.name: led_endless
request.description: The compositor will run the given effect until a `led_temporary`, another `led_endless`, or `stop_led` request supersedes it.

event.name: configure
event.description: Delivered once on surface creation. Carries the widget's size class and its pixel dimensions. Follow-up `param_*` and setting events refine configuration; the batch is terminated by `configure_done`.

event.name: display_info
event.description:
Delivered once on surface creation, after `configure` and before `configure_done`. Carries the active display's logical pixel size, shape, and DPI so widgets can branch on real geometry instead of the legacy `size_type`. DPI is the platform's real display density and is advisory during this development stage.
Widgets that do not bind this event ignore it; old widgets keep working unchanged.

event.name: params
event.description:
The widget's per-instance params, exactly as stored in the scene configuration. A JSON-encoded object whose keys and value types match the widget's manifest. The compositor does not parse or validate this — the widget owns its manifest and is authoritative on what values are meaningful.
Emitted on surface creation as part of the initial configure batch, and re-emitted at runtime whenever the widget's params change (via an update that keeps the widget's geometry stable). An empty JSON object ("{}") is sent when no params are configured.

event.name: configure_done
event.description: Terminates the initial configure batch. After this event the widget has every piece of initial configuration the compositor intends to deliver and may start rendering. Subsequent setting events represent runtime changes.

event.name: timezone
event.description: Current timezone, IANA identifier (e.g. "Europe/Prague"). Sent on connect and whenever the timezone changes.

event.name: night_mode
event.description: Whether night mode is active. Sent on connect and on toggle.

event.name: next_alarm
event.description:
Soonest upcoming alarm derived host-side from the operator's alarm list. Sent on connect and whenever the next-to-fire entry changes (alarm add/edit/delete/fire/snooze, or timezone change).
`fire_at_utc_ms_hi` and `fire_at_utc_ms_lo` carry the high and low 32 bits of a signed 64-bit milliseconds-since-UNIX-epoch timestamp, matching the hi/lo split pattern from wp_presentation_feedback. Both args are zero when `present` is `absent`.

arg.name: fire_at_utc_ms_hi
arg.summary: high 32 bits of the signed 64-bit ms timestamp

arg.name: fire_at_utc_ms_lo
arg.summary: low 32 bits of the signed 64-bit ms timestamp

arg.name: name

event.name: lifecycle
event.description:
Emitted whenever the widget's lifecycle state changes. The initial emission immediately after the configure_done batch is always one of the idle states: 'dormant', 'prepared', or 'visible'. The transitional states 'entering' and 'leaving' only appear during an active scene-cycle drag, never as a first event.
Within a scene change the compositor emits a release batch (transitions into 'dormant') and flushes it, then emits the acquire batch (all other transitions) and flushes again. This ordering lets a shared render-target pool be reclaimed before the next acquire and is the only ordering guarantee the compositor makes between batches.
Permitted transitions (the compositor never emits anything else): dormant -> prepared | visible | entering prepared -> dormant | visible | entering visible -> dormant | prepared | leaving entering -> visible | prepared | dormant leaving -> dormant | prepared | visible
Widgets that do not bind this event silently ignore it; old widgets keep working unchanged.

event.name: shutdown
event.description: Sent when the widget should shut down gracefully. Widget should clean up and exit.

enum.name: lifecycle_state
enum.description: Tracks whether the widget is on-screen, neighbouring an on-screen widget, transitioning in or out under a scene-cycle drag, or completely off-screen. The host runtime uses this to acquire and release render-target buffers and to gate animation ticking.

enum.name: display_shape
enum.description: Shape of the visible display area. Advisory layout metadata; the widget coordinate space stays rectangular regardless of shape.
